summary: bundle-aware skill content authority (cinatra#2088, epic #2086 S1) — the operator-upgrade twin of the fresh-install bootstrap DDL (skillBundleSchemaQueries in src/lib/skill-lifecycle-schema.ts, spread into buildCreateStoreSchemaQueries in the SAME PR). Turns the single-blob content authority (core__0031's skill_revision_contents, one immutable UTF-8 text blob per revision) into a multi-file, binary-capable bundle authority. skill_bundle_blobs: a RAW-BYTE (bytea) content-addressable blob store keyed by encode(sha256(content),'hex'), uniform for text AND binary resources so a non-UTF-8 reference (an image, a compiled fixture) survives byte-exact where the text-column skill_revision_contents could not; two DB CHECKs make a wrong blob impossible (content_digest = sha256(content); byte_length = octet_length(content)) and a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger enforces append-only (a blob is a pure function of its digest). skill_revision_files: the immutable revision-file MANIFEST — one row per (revision_id, path) binding a bundled file's normalized path to its content_digest (into skill_bundle_blobs), byte_length, unix mode (0o644=420 default), and an is_router flag distinguishing the single SKILL.md; PRIMARY KEY (revision_id, path); a path CHECK rejects absolute / backslash / '..'-traversal paths (POSIX-normalized before insert) and a router CHECK binds is_router => path='SKILL.md'; skill_id + content_digest indexes; append-only trigger. skill_revisions.bundle_digest: the revision identity (the deterministic digest over the sorted (path, content_digest) set computed by the pure computeBundleDigest), nullable — a pre-S1 revision is NULL until its bundle is ingested at runtime. skill_bundle_heads: the bundle authority's CURRENT-BUNDLE pointer, one row per skill (skill_id -> revision_id, bundle_digest), deliberately mutable like skills.active_revision_id — it is what lets a DERIVED (extension/package) skill, which never gets a lifecycle revision, carry a bundle identity at all. anthropic_skill_sync.revision_id + .bundle_digest: the byte-bound sync binding recording WHICH stored revision (and its bundle identity) the uploaded bytes were derived from, so drift is a pure manifest comparison and never a disk re-hash; nullable so an already-provisioned namespace upgrades additively and is populated on the next byte-bound sync. NO foreign keys on skill_revision_files (revision_id/skill_id) ON PURPOSE — the skill_revisions precedent: durable history that survives a hard skill delete, and an ON DELETE CASCADE would fire the append-only trigger during a catalog-replace and abort the whole transaction. ADDITIVE + IDEMPOTENT — three brand-new tables (skill_bundle_blobs and skill_revision_files with their append-only triggers, plus the MUTABLE pointer table skill_bundle_heads) plus three ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS; DDL MIRRORS the bootstrap leaf exactly (CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS): a no-op on a bootstrap-seeded schema, ledger-faked on a fresh install, executed by db migrate on an existing deployment; unqualified names ride the runner's search_path (the app schema). NO backfill: bytea content is not derivable from SQL (it lives on disk), so pre-S1 skills are captured lazily+idempotently at runtime (the sync CAPTURE phase, which seeds an existing lifecycle head before considering disk — the one-time remote re-baseline). down() drops the three fresh tables (skill_bundle_heads, then children first: skill_revision_files then skill_bundle_blobs) plus their trigger/function and the three added columns (loses bundle rows + the byte-bound binding by design; the legacy single-blob content authority + content-hash sync remain fully intact, so nothing else depends on these objects at S1; empty on a fresh install). SEQ 0084 — strictly greater than the max shipped seq on origin/main (core__0083); a concurrent lane may land the next seq first, in which case a rename-only renumber is normal (FLAGGED for the coordinator's train). migrations/** is HIGH-RISK: owner approval required; the lane never merges.
